{"statements":{"L5.1":{"established":"yes","quote":"For $f(x)=x+c$ ($c\ge 0$) the original inequalities become  

\[
\sqrt{\frac{x^2 + (y+c)^2}{2}} \ge \frac{x+y+c}{2} \ge \sqrt{x(y+c)} ,
\]

which are exactly the Quadratic‑Mean–Arithmetic‑Mean inequality and the Arithmetic‑Mean–Geometric‑Mean inequality","note":"Both inequalities are verified for all positive x,y and every c≥0."},"L5.2":{"established":"yes","quote":"Taking square roots (all terms are positive) yields  

\[
f(f(y)) + y = 2f(y) \qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad 
\boxed{f(f(x)) = 2f(x) - x \qquad \forall x>0.}","note":"The structural identity is correctly derived from the collapsed chain."},"L5.3":{"established":"no","quote":null,"note":"The proof never shows that positivity of all iterates forces g(x)≥0; negative values are simply omitted."},"L5.4":{"established":"yes","quote":"Suppose $V$ contains two distinct positive numbers $c_1 > c_2 > 0$... From the functional equation (4) we obtain  

\[
g(u + n c_1) = c_1,\qquad g(v + m c_2) = c_2
\]
... Thus $V$ contains **at most one** positive number.","note":"The rational and irrational ratio cases give an iterative contradiction for two distinct positive differences."},"L5.5":{"established":"partial","quote":"From (11) we immediately obtain $(x-y)^2 > c^2$, hence  

\[
|x-y| > c \qquad \forall\,x\in S_0,\;y\in S_c .
\]","note":"Fixed/non-fixed separation and covering are proved only after the unsupported assertion V⊆{0,c}; negative differences were never excluded."}},"S_ref":1,"notes":"Sufficiency is complete. Necessity has a fatal missing step: it never proves g(x)≥0, yet concludes that at most one positive value implies V⊆{0,c}. Thus the fixed-point argument is only conditional."}
